{{Short description|German chemist (1928–1974)}}
'''Gerhard Raspé''' (born 20 January 1928 in [[Bucharest]], died 1 September 1974 in [[West Berlin]]) was a Romanian-born German [[organic chemistry|organic chemist]], who served as research director at [[Schering AG]] and a member of the company's [[Vorstand|executive board]].

[[File:Grab Gerhard Raspé.jpg|thumb|Grave of Gerhard Raspé at [[Friedhof Heerstraße]], Berlin]]

== Education and career ==
Following his studies of organic chemistry at the [[Braunschweig University of Technology|Brunswick University of Technology]] and the [[Complutense University of Madrid|University of Madrid]], he obtained a doctorate in chemistry (Dr.rer.nat.) and worked as a researcher in the field of [[steroid hormone]]s and [[biochemistry]] at the pharmaceutical company [[Schering AG]]. In 1964, he became a member of the [[Vorstand|executive board]] of Schering and the company's director of research.<ref>''Schering Symposium on Endocrinology'', Berlin, May 26 to 27, 1967: Advances in The Biosciences, p. 307, Elsevier, 2013</ref> He was a board member of the [[Max Planck Society]]<ref>''Naturwissenschaftliche Rundschau'', vol. 27, p. 470</ref> and a member of the [[German Council of Science and Humanities]]. He died in 1974, aged 46.<ref>''Chemische industrie: Zeitschrift für die deutsche Chemiewirtschaft'', vol. 26, p. 696, 1974</ref>
